newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Carrier seeks Tadiran Appliances stake.
newsitem.headline: Carrier seeks Tadiran Appliances stake.

text.p: Israel's Tadiran Ltd is in negotiations with Carrier Corp to sell the U.S. company a 27 percent stake in its Tadiran Electrical Appliances Ltd unit, a Tadiran official said on Wednesday.
In December, a Tadiran official said there were negotiations with a foreign company but refused to name it.

Israel's Haaretz daily said on Wednesday that Tadiran and Carrier -- a subsidiary of United Technologies Corp and the world's biggest producer of heating and air-conditioning systems -- were on the verge of signing a deal.
A Tadiran spokesman refused to comment on the Haaretz report, but a company official who spoke on condition of anonymity confirmed there were talks with Carrier.

Haaretz said Carrier would pay $18 million for Tadiran Appliances and would have an option to buy an additional 24 percent stake within three years. Exercising the option would give it control of the company, a manufacturer and importer of air conditioners, refrigerators and other appliances.
At Tadiran Appliances' current market value, the Carrier stake would be worth $13 million.
Tadiran Ltd, which controls 88 percent of Tadiran Appliances, has been seeking strategic partners for its various subsidiary companies, most of which deal in telecommunications and electronics.
On February 19, Tadiran announced that IBM Israel had agreed to acquire a 51 percent stake in its Tadiran Information Systems for $9.4 million in cash and assets.
